requirement.text: Each thermostat shall have a unique identifier by which that thermostat is identified in the THEMAS system.

classification.rationale: The requirement specifies device identification for thermostats within an IoT or hardware management system (THEMAS), which does not explicitly indicate a web application, mobile application, or machine-learning system.

rounds.text_checked: Each thermostat shall have a unique identifier by which that thermostat is identified in the THEMAS system.

test_strategy.rationale: Equivalence partitioning applies to test valid unique identifiers, duplicate identifiers (violating the uniqueness constraint), and invalid/malformed identifiers. Exploratory testing applies as the requirement lacks explicit numeric ranges, state transitions, or multi-step workflow details, allowing testers to explore edge cases in identifier assignment, collision handling, and retrieval.

test_cases.title: Valid Unique Thermostat Identifier Registration and Retrieval
test_cases.preconditions: THEMAS system is operational and ready to accept thermostat registrations.
steps: Register a new thermostat with a unique identifier 'THERM-00100'.
Submit a system query to retrieve thermostat details using identifier 'THERM-00100'.
test_cases.expected_result: The thermostat is successfully registered and correctly retrieved from the THEMAS system using its unique identifier.

test_cases.title: Duplicate Thermostat Identifier Rejection
test_cases.preconditions: A thermostat with identifier 'THERM-00101' is already registered in THEMAS.
steps: Attempt to register a second thermostat using the existing identifier 'THERM-00101'.
test_cases.expected_result: The system rejects the registration request with a clear error indicating the identifier is already in use and must be unique.

test_cases.title: Missing or Null Thermostat Identifier Validation
steps: Attempt to register a thermostat with an empty string or null identifier.
test_cases.expected_result: The registration fails with a validation error indicating that a unique identifier is mandatory for each thermostat.

test_cases.title: Concurrent Thermostat Registration Race Condition Handling
test_cases.preconditions: THEMAS system API is accessible concurrently from multiple clients.
steps: Initiate two parallel registration requests for different thermostats using the same identifier 'THERM-CONCUR-01' at the exact same millisecond.
Inspect the system state and response codes for both requests.
test_cases.expected_result: Exactly one registration request succeeds and the other fails with a uniqueness collision error. The system maintains single-thermostat mapping for 'THERM-CONCUR-01'.

test_cases.title: Exploratory Identifier Case Sensitivity and Boundary Characters
steps: Attempt to register another thermostat with identifier 'THERM-123-ABC' (case variation).
Query device status for both upper-case and lower-case identifiers.
test_cases.expected_result: The system handles identifier case-sensitivity strictly and deterministically according to system specifications, preventing identifier collisions or ambiguous device lookups.

final_text: Each thermostat shall have a unique identifier by which that thermostat is identified in the THEMAS system.
